We need retrosynthesis route for target: Cc1ccc(NS(=O)(=O)c2ccc(/C=C/C(=O)Nc3ccccc3N)cc2)cc1

We need up to 3 steps, leaves must be commercially available, total price <=9999 (we can't check price but assume typical). Need to propose route using templates.

We need to find disconnections: The molecule has a sulfonamide linking two aromatic rings, and an amide attached to a phenyl with an aniline (NH2) on that phenyl. Also a trans-alkene linking amide phenyl to sulfonyl phenyl.

Potential retrosynthesis: Break sulfonamide to give sulfonyl chloride (or sulfonyl aryl) and aniline. Also break amide to give acid chloride and aniline.

Step 1: Disconnection at sulfonamide: target -> sulfonyl chloride (aryl-SO2Cl) + aniline (para-methyl phenyl amine). The sulfonyl chloride could be commercially available: p-tolylsulfonyl chloride (CH3C6H4SO2Cl). The aniline part is the other aromatic ring with amide side chain: maybe 4-(E-... )? Actually the sulfonamide nitrogen attached to the first phenyl (tolyl) and to the second phenyl (sulfonyl attached to second phenyl). Wait structure: Cc1ccc(N S(=O)(=O) c2ccc(/C=C/C(=O)Nc3ccccc3N)cc2)cc1. So sulfonamide nitrogen attached to tolyl (para-methyl phenyl) and to sulfonyl attached to second phenyl (which has the side chain). So sulfonamide nitrogen is connecting both aromatic rings. So disconnection could give p-toluidine (para-methyl aniline) and sulfonyl chloride of second phenyl (Ar-SO2Cl). Then combine via sulfonyl chloride + amine to form sulfonamide.

Thus step 1: p-toluidine (commercial) + 4-(E-... )-phenylsulfonyl chloride (maybe not commercial). Might need to make sulfonyl chloride from sulfonic acid (commercial) via SOCl2.

Alternative: Disconnection at amide: break amide to give aniline (c3ccccc3N) and acid chloride of the alkene side chain (C= C C(=O)Cl). The acid chloride could be 4-(E)-3-(chlorocarbonyl)but-2-enoic? Actually the side chain is /C=C/C(=O)N-Ph-NH2. So acid chloride would be trans-2-chlorobut-2-enoic acid chloride? Wait: The amide carbonyl attached to the alkene carbon (alpha,beta-unsaturated). So the acid chloride would be trans-2-chlorobut-2-enoic acid chloride? Actually the carbonyl carbon is attached to the alkene carbon (C= C - C(=O) - N). So the acid chloride would be trans-2-chloroacryloyl chloride? The structure: /C=C/C(=O)N-Ph-NH2. So the acid chloride is trans-2-chloroacryloyl chloride? No chlorine not present. It's just acryloyl chloride (CH2=CH-COCl) but with trans geometry and attached to phenyl? Wait the alkene is attached to phenyl sulfonyl side: c2ccc(/C=C/C(=O)Nc3ccccc3N)cc2. So the alkene carbon attached to phenyl ring (aryl-CH=CH-CO-NH-Ph-NH2). So the acid chloride would be trans-2-phenylacryloyl chloride? Actually the alkene is attached to phenyl ring at the beta carbon: Ar-CH=CH-CO-... So acid chloride would be trans-2-phenylacryloyl chloride (Ar-CH=CH-COCl). That may be commercially available.

Thus route: Step 1: Form amide between trans-2-phenylacryloyl chloride and 4-aminophenyl (c3ccccc3N). That gives the side chain amide with aniline. Then step 2: sulfonylate the aniline (the nitrogen of sulfonamide) with p-toluenesulfonyl chloride? Wait the sulfonamide nitrogen is the same as the aniline that is part of the amide? Actually the amide nitrogen is attached to phenyl (c3ccccc3N) which is an aniline (para? not). That nitrogen is part of amide, not the sulfonamide. The sulfonamide nitrogen is separate (attached to tolyl and sulfonyl phenyl). So we have two different nitrogens.

Thus we need to connect the sulfonamide after amide formation. The sulfonamide nitrogen is the aniline of the tolyl ring (p-toluidine). So we need p-toluidine to react with sulfonyl chloride of the second phenyl (which already contains the amide side chain). So we need to first make the sulfonyl chloride of the second phenyl (aryl-SO2Cl) from the corresponding sulfonic acid (aryl-SO3H) maybe commercial. Then couple with p-toluidine to give sulfonamide.

Thus overall steps:

1. Synthesize amide: React trans-2-phenylacryloyl chloride (commercial) with 4-aminophenyl (aniline) (c3ccccc3N) to give (E)-4-(phenylamido)but-2-enoic? Actually product: /C=C/C(=O)Nc3ccccc3N (the amide). This yields the side chain attached to phenyl sulfonyl ring? Wait the phenyl sulfonyl ring is the one bearing the side chain. So we need to attach the amide to that phenyl ring via the alkene substituent. The phenyl ring is the same as the sulfonyl phenyl. So we need to start from that phenyl ring with a substituent of trans-CH=CH-COCl (acryloyl chloride). So we need 4-(E)-(2-chloro?) Actually we need 4-(E)-CH=CH-COCl attached to phenyl. That is 4-(E)-2-chloro? Not.

Thus we could start from 4-(E)-styryl carboxylic acid? Actually we need phenyl-CH=CH-COCl. That's 4-(E)-cinnamoyl chloride (cinnamoyl chloride). Cinnamoyl chloride is commercially available (C6H5-CH=CH-COCl). Good.

So step 1: React cinnamoyl chloride with 4-aminophenyl (aniline) to give (E)-cinnamoyl anilide (C= C C(=O)N-Ph). That yields the side chain attached to phenyl (the phenyl is the aniline). Wait the aniline is the phenyl that will later be attached to sulfonyl? Actually the amide attaches to the phenyl that is part of the sulfonyl phenyl? The target has phenyl (c3ccccc3N) attached to amide nitrogen, not to the carbonyl carbon. So the amide nitrogen is attached to phenyl (aniline). So the amide is formed between cinnamoyl chloride and aniline (c3ccccc3N). That gives product: C6H5-CH=CH-CO-NH-C6H4-NH2 (para? Actually the aniline is unsubstituted phenyl with NH2). In target, the phenyl attached to amide nitrogen also has an NH2 at para? The SMILES: Nc3ccccc3N indicates an aniline with two nitrogens? Actually "Nc3ccccc3N" means an aniline where the nitrogen attached to carbonyl is attached to the phenyl at position 1, and there is another NH2 at the other end? Wait "Nc3ccccc3N" is an aniline with an NH attached to the phenyl at position 1 (the amide nitrogen) and also an NH2 at the other end? The SMILES "Nc3ccccc3N" means the phenyl has an NH attached at one carbon (the one attached to carbonyl) and also an NH2 at the other end? Actually "Nc3ccccc3N" is a phenyl with two substituents: an N attached to the carbonyl (as part of amide) and an N (NH2) at the other end (para?). The SMILES: N c3 c c c c c3 N. The first N is attached to the aromatic carbon (position 1) and the last N is attached to the aromatic carbon (position 6). So it's 1,6-diaminobenzene (p-phenylenediamine). So the amide nitrogen is attached to one amino group of p-phenylenediamine, leaving the other amino group free.

Thus the amide formation uses p-phenylenediamine (1,4-diaminobenzene) maybe? Actually positions 1 and 6 are ortho? In SMILES, the ring numbering is sequential; "c3ccccc3" is a phenyl; preceding "N" attaches to first carbon, trailing "N" attaches to last carbon (which is same as first due to ring closure? Actually the SMILES "c3ccccc3" defines a benzene ring; preceding "N" attaches to the first aromatic carbon; trailing "N" attaches to the last aromatic carbon which is the same as the first due to closure? No, the last "N" after the ring closure attaches to the same carbon as the first? In SMILES, "c1ccccc1" is a ring; if you write "Nc1ccccc1N", the first N attaches to carbon 1, the second N attaches to carbon 1 as well? Actually both N's attach to the same carbon because after closure you are back at the same atom. So "Nc1ccccc1N" is an aniline with two N attached to same carbon, which is impossible. So likely the SMILES is "Nc3ccccc3N" meaning an aniline with an NH attached to the aromatic carbon (position 1) and an NH2 attached to the same carbon? That seems wrong. But maybe the SMILES is misinterpreted; but we can treat it as p-phenylenediamine (1,4-diaminobenzene) which is common.

Thus we need p-phenylenediamine (commercial) as starting material.

Thus step 1: Cinnamoyl chloride + p-phenylenediamine -> amide (mono-acylated) giving product with one free NH2.

Step 2: Sulfonylation: React p-toluidine (or the other aromatic ring) with 4-(E)-cinnamoyl-p-phenylenediamine sulfonyl chloride? Wait the sulfonyl chloride is attached to the phenyl that already has the amide side chain. So we need to generate aryl sulfonyl chloride of that phenyl (the same phenyl as the amide). That phenyl is the one bearing the amide side chain (c2ccc(... )cc2). So we need to start from that phenyl sulfonic acid (or sulfonyl chloride) which also has the amide side chain attached. That could be synthesized after step 1: we have the phenyl with amide side chain (c2ccc(C=CC(=O)NPhNH2)cc2). Then we need to sulfonylate that phenyl (introduce SO2Cl) at para position relative to side chain? In target, the sulfonyl group is attached to that phenyl at para position (since the sulfonamide nitrogen attaches to that phenyl). So we need to introduce sulfonyl chloride at para position of that phenyl. That could be done via sulfonation of the aromatic ring (e.g., using chlorosulfonic acid) to give aryl sulfonyl chloride. That may be feasible but not via template.

Simplify: Use commercially available 4-(E)-cinnamoylbenzenesulfonyl chloride? Might be available. Search.

Let's try search for template for sulfonylation of aniline? But we need to produce sulfonamide linking two aromatic rings. Could also reverse: first form sulfonamide between p-toluidine and 4-(E)-cinnamoylbenzenesulfonyl chloride (commercial). Then amide formation on the second phenyl's side chain using p-phenylenediamine? Wait the sulfonyl chloride already has the amide side chain attached? That would be 4-(E)-cinnamoylbenzenesulfonyl chloride (aryl-SO2Cl with cinnamoyl substituent). Then reacting with p-toluidine gives sulfonamide linking to tolyl. Then we need to attach the second aniline (p-phenylenediamine) to the amide carbonyl. But the amide carbonyl is already present in the sulfonyl chloride precursor? Actually the sulfonyl chloride precursor would have the amide side chain already formed? No, the amide side chain is attached to the phenyl via the alkene and carbonyl, not via sulfonyl. So the sulfonyl chloride precursor could be 4-(E)-cinnamoylbenzenesulfonyl chloride (aryl-SO2Cl with cinnamoyl substituent). That is a single molecule containing both the alkene and sulfonyl chloride. Then we can react with p-toluidine to give sulfonamide, and then we need to attach the aniline (p-phenylenediamine) to the amide carbonyl? Actually the amide carbonyl is already part of the cinnamoyl group; we need to convert the acid chloride of cinnamoyl to amide with p-phenylenediamine. But the sulfonyl chloride precursor has a carbonyl as part of the cinnamoyl group (C=O) attached to the alkene, not as acid chloride. So we need to convert that carbonyl to amide later via activation (e.g., using coupling reagents). That's more steps.

Given limited steps, maybe propose 2-step route: 1) Couple p-toluidine with 4-(E)-cinnamoylbenzenesulfonyl chloride to form sulfonamide. 2) Amidation of the cinnamoyl carbonyl with p-phenylenediamine using standard coupling (e.g., EDC). That's 2 steps.

Assume both reagents are commercially available: p-toluidine, 4-(E)-cinnamoylbenzenesulfonyl chloride, p-phenylenediamine. Check buyability.

Let's test is_buyable for these SMILES.

We need SMILES for p-toluidine: Cc1ccc(N)cc1

Cinnamoyl benzenesulfonyl chloride: The SMILES: O=S(=O)(Cl)c1ccc(C=CC(=O)Cl)cc1? Wait carbonyl is acid chloride? Actually cinnamoyl chloride is C=CC(=O)Cl attached to phenyl. So combine with sulfonyl chloride: O=S(=O)(Cl)c1ccc(C=CC(=O)Cl)cc1

SMILES: O=S(=O)(Cl)c1ccc(C=CC(=O)Cl)cc1

p-phenylenediamine: Nc1ccccc1N

Let's check buyability.
